entrypoint_protocol: argv CLI executed with `python todo.py`; optional global `--data-file PATH` precedes one of the `add`, `list`, `done`, or `stats` subcommands
objective: Build a robust multi-file argv todo CLI with persistent local JSON state, add/list/done/stats commands, helpful errors, and real automated tests.
public_behavior_spec: The CLI is invoked as `python todo.py [--data-file PATH] COMMAND [ARGS]` and must not require third-party packages.
If `--data-file` is omitted, state is stored in `.todo.json` in the current working directory. Commands using the same data-file path must observe state written by earlier processes.
`add TITLE` trims leading and trailing whitespace, assigns a stable monotonically increasing positive integer ID, persists a pending todo, and prints `Added #ID: TITLE`.
`list` prints every todo in ascending ID order. Pending items use `[ ] #ID TITLE`, completed items use `[x] #ID TITLE`, and an empty store prints `No todos.`.
`done ID` persists the matching todo as completed and prints `Completed #ID: TITLE`.
`stats` prints separate `Total: N`, `Pending: N`, and `Completed: N` lines derived from persisted state.

The state file is valid JSON and retains enough information to preserve todo IDs, titles, completion status, and the next ID across invocations. State updates should avoid leaving a partially written file.

A whitespace-only title and syntactically invalid arguments are usage errors with exit status 2 and a diagnostic beginning with `Error:`. Unknown IDs, already-completed todos, unreadable state, and malformed state are operational errors with a nonzero exit status and a helpful diagnostic beginning with `Error:`.
Malformed or incompatible JSON state must not be silently discarded or overwritten.
`--help` exits successfully and identifies the add, list, done, and stats commands.
The implementation is split into an argv entry module, command handling, and JSON persistence modules rather than placing all behavior in one file.
The repository includes automated tests that execute the CLI in separate processes and cover persistence, the main command lifecycle, statistics, and error behavior.

public_tests.description: The argv entrypoint exposes all required commands in its help output.
Listing a fresh explicitly selected store produces a clear empty-state message.
Adds, completion state, listing, and statistics persist across independent CLI invocations.
Completing an unknown ID fails with a specific helpful diagnostic.
A whitespace-only title is rejected as a usage error rather than persisted.
Named integration tests supplied with the project execute successfully.

qualitative_rubric: Core credit requires the public commands to execute successfully; documentation or prose claims do not substitute for observable behavior.
Persistence quality is judged by separate-process behavior, valid JSON output, stable IDs, and preservation of existing state after failures.
Error quality is judged by nonzero exit statuses and diagnostics that identify the failed operation or input without exposing a traceback during ordinary user errors.
Architecture quality is judged by whether command parsing, domain behavior, and storage concerns are meaningfully separated while retaining a small, understandable entrypoint.
Test quality is judged by automated subprocess-based coverage using isolated temporary state files, including successful lifecycle behavior and representative failures.
The implementation should remain portable across standard Python environments and avoid machine-specific paths, network services, and undeclared dependencies.
stopping_condition: Stop when all required artifacts exist, every public executable test passes from the candidate root, persistence and error behavior satisfy the public specification, and the manager determines whether the result is released.
